findings.title: schema/finding.schema.json is never validated against, and the self-test built to catch that passes on a coincidental substring match
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:338-340 (findings.json entries built and frozen with no validate() call)
test/schemas.jl:88-98 ("every shipped schema is read by something")
findings.description: `load_schema("finding")` and `validate(load_schema("finding"), ...)` occur nowhere in src/ or ext/ (checked by exhaustive grep of every `load_schema(` call site: config, round, audit, exemptions, managed, ground-truth, reproduction, pass, tally, dismissal, hat — never finding). Every sibling round artefact (ROUND.toml, tally.json, pass.toml, audit.json, dismissal output, ground_truth.json, reproductions/*.json) is schema-validated at the point it is written (Rounds.jl:41/350/426, Preflight.jl:574, Passes.jl:86/155/315/473, Audit.jl:44), but the id-bearing findings.json entries assembled at Rounds.jl:338-340 and frozen at line 366-368 are written with no such call, even though schema/finding.schema.json's own title says it is 'the ONE shape of the fleet' and documents exactly those fields (id, seeded, seed_class added to the base finding). The gap is invisible because test/schemas.jl's own liveness check is satisfied for name="finding" by the unrelated literal `e["scope"] == "finding"` in Doctor.jl:306, Preflight.jl:398, Passes.jl:178/391/510 (ledger scope comparisons, nothing to do with the finding schema), so the test reports the schema as 'read' when it is not.
findings.resolution_hint: Either call validate(load_schema("finding"), f) at the point findings.json is frozen in Rounds.jl bank(), or delete schema/finding.schema.json as redundant. Separately, tighten test/schemas.jl's liveness test to require load_schema("<name>") literally rather than a bare substring match.

findings.title: instruments/bug-hunt/schema.json carries two dead $defs blocks (finding, hunt_finding) that duplicate — and have already drifted from — the live inline schema
findings.description: grep -c '$ref' instruments/bug-hunt/schema.json returns 0 — the file contains no $ref anywhere, so its two $defs entries are unreachable dead code; the schema instead spells the same shape out a third time inline under lane_file.properties.findings.items (the one classify_lane actually validates against, via instrument_schema(inst)). The dead $defs.finding has already drifted from the live copy: it lacks kind/verdict/observed/file/line/mechanism entirely and its own required list omits them.
findings.resolution_hint: Make the inline lane_file.properties.findings.items an allOf/$ref to #/$defs/hunt_finding (the complete shape) and delete the now-redundant $defs.finding, mirroring how check-docs/check-consistency/audit-changes correctly $ref their own $defs.finding.

findings.title: managed.schema.json and tally.schema.json define a $defs.entry documenting per-key shape but never wire it in, so the dynamic maps they describe go unchecked
locations: src/CLI/Schema.jl:136-142 (additionalProperties as a schema Dict IS supported by validate())
findings.description: grep -rn '#/$defs/entry' schema/*.schema.json instruments/*/schema.json returns nothing: neither file's $defs.entry is ever $ref'd. Both 'files' (managed.schema.json) and 'per_id' (tally.schema.json) are declared with additionalProperties: true, required: [], properties: {} — so a malformed entry (missing sha256, invalid act/closed_by enum value) passes validation silently. The validator already supports a schema as additionalProperties (config.schema.json's 'paths', audit-changes' 'executable_claims'), so additionalProperties: {"$ref": "#/$defs/entry"} would actually enforce it.
findings.resolution_hint: Change 'files' in managed.schema.json and 'per_id' in tally.schema.json from additionalProperties: true to additionalProperties: {"$ref": "#/$defs/entry"}.

findings.title: exemptions.schema.json's reason minLength (24) is looser than what CFG.EXEMPTIONS actually enforces (40, for every entry)
locations: schema/exemptions.schema.json:61-65 (reason minLength: 24, description claims '≥ 40 chars on scope finding')
findings.description: The schema sets reason to minLength: 24 and its description claims the 40-character floor applies only 'on scope finding'. But Doctor.jl:305 runs length(e["reason"]) >= 40 unconditionally, inside the for e in ctx.ledger loop, before the if e["scope"] == "finding" branch at line 306 — every ledger entry of every scope is held to 40 characters. A reason of 24-39 characters therefore validates against the schema but is unconditionally rejected by gbg doctor's CFG.EXEMPTIONS check, and the schema's own comment misdescribes which entries the bound applies to.
findings.resolution_hint: Raise reason's minLength to 40 in exemptions.schema.json and correct the description to drop 'on scope finding'.
